items.q: Orphan Annie eye nuclei, nuclear grooves and psammoma bodies indicate which thyroid cancer?
items.exp: Papillary carcinoma shows optically clear orphan Annie nuclei, grooves, pseudoinclusions and laminated psammoma bodies, spreading lymphatically with excellent prognosis despite nodal disease.
r: Incorrect. Follicular cancer is judged by invasion, not these nuclei.
Correct. These nuclear features mean papillary carcinoma.
Incorrect. Medullary shows amyloid and calcitonin instead.
Incorrect. Anaplastic is undifferentiated and rapidly lethal.
items.kp: Clear nuclei plus psammoma bodies equal papillary cancer.

items.q: Why can cytology not diagnose follicular carcinoma?
o: Diagnosis requires capsular or vascular invasion seen only histologically
items.exp: Follicular adenoma and carcinoma share cytology; malignancy is defined by invasion through capsule or into vessels on excised histology. Aspirates therefore report follicular neoplasm needing surgery for verdict.
r: Incorrect. Cells may look atypical without proving invasion.
Correct. Invasion on histology defines follicular cancer.
Incorrect. Aspirates sample follicular lesions readily.
Incorrect. Calcitonin marks medullary, not follicular, disease.
items.kp: No invasion seen, no follicular cancer called.

items.q: Calcitonin secreting thyroid cancer with amyloid stroma arising from C cells is what?
items.exp: Medullary carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells, secretes calcitonin (and CEA), deposits amyloid and occurs sporadically or in MEN2 with RET mutations needing family screening.
r: Incorrect. Papillary arises from follicular cells with orphan nuclei.
Correct. C cell calcitonin cancer is medullary.
Incorrect. Follicular cancers secrete thyroglobulin lineage markers.
Incorrect. Hurthle adenoma is a benign follicular variant.
items.kp: Calcitonin plus amyloid plus MEN2 equals medullary cancer.

items.q: Painless goitre drifting to hypothyroidism with lymphoid germinal centres and Hurthle cells indicates what?
items.exp: Hashimoto thyroiditis infiltrates the gland with lymphocytes, plasma cells and germinal centres, Hurthle metaplasia and fibrosis, progressing to hypothyroidism with anti TPO antibodies.
r: Incorrect. Graves stimulates hyperthyroidism with diffuse hyperplasia.
Correct. Hashimoto destroys toward hypothyroidism.
Incorrect. Subacute disease is painful and transiently toxic.
Incorrect. Riedel is woody invasive fibrosis, rare.
items.kp: Lymphocytes plus Hurthle plus hypothyroid drift: Hashimoto.

items.q: Hyperthyroidism with diffuse goitre, ophthalmopathy and pretibial myxoedema is caused by what mechanism?
items.exp: Graves antibodies stimulate the TSH receptor driving hormone overproduction plus orbital and skin changes from shared antigen expression. Destructive thyroiditis lacks eye disease and shows low uptake.
r: Incorrect. Leak causes transient thyrotoxicosis without eye signs.
Correct. Stimulating receptor antibodies cause Graves disease.
Incorrect. Factitious intake suppresses the gland without goitre eye signs.
Incorrect. Single toxic adenoma lacks diffuse eye disease.
items.kp: Eye disease plus diffuse toxic goitre equals Graves until disproven.

items.q: High calcium, low phosphate and raised PTH with kidney stones most likely reflect what?
items.exp: Primary hyperparathyroidism (usually one adenoma) raises PTH driven calcium with phosphate wasting and stones. Malignancy and vitamin D causes suppress PTH, the key split.
r: Incorrect. PTHrP suppresses native PTH measurement.
Correct. Raised PTH with high calcium means parathyroid disease.
Incorrect. Vitamin D excess suppresses PTH too.
Incorrect. Sarcoid calcitriol also suppresses PTH.
items.kp: Calcium up with PTH up: parathyroid. PTH down: hunt cancer or vitamins.

items.q: Post thyroidectomy tingling, carpopedal spasm and prolonged QT indicate which complication?
items.exp: Parathyroid removal or devascularisation drops PTH and calcium causing perioral tingling, Chvostek and Trousseau signs, seizures and QT prolongation needing calcium replacement.
r: Incorrect. Nerve injury changes voice, not calcium signs.
Correct. Low calcium from hypoparathyroidism causes spasm.
Incorrect. Storm causes fever and tachycardia hypermetabolism.
Incorrect. Superior nerve injury alters pitch only.
items.kp: Spasm after thyroid surgery equals lost parathyroids. Check calcium.

items.q: Short fourth metacarpals, obesity and PTH resistance with high PTH and low calcium define what?
items.exp: Pseudohypoparathyroidism (Albright hereditary osteodystrophy) resists PTH at receptor signalling (GNAS) so PTH is high yet calcium low, with short metacarpals and round facies.
r: Incorrect. Surgical loss gives low PTH, not resistance high PTH.
Correct. Hormone resistance with skeletal signs is pseudohypoparathyroidism.
Incorrect. Primary overactivity raises calcium instead.
Incorrect. Vitamin D lack lacks the metacarpal phenotype.
items.kp: High PTH but low calcium plus short fingers: hormone resistance.

items.q: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma characteristically presents how?
o: Slow painless nodule in a young woman
Rapidly enlarging hard invasive neck mass in an elderly patient
items.exp: Anaplastic carcinoma is undifferentiated, rapidly invades airway and vessels in elderly patients and carries dismal prognosis, often arising from long standing differentiated cancer or goitre.
r: Incorrect. Slow young nodules suggest benign or papillary disease.
Correct. Rapid invasive elderly mass means anaplastic until proven otherwise.
Incorrect. Toxic goitre is Graves or nodular hyperfunction.
Incorrect. Incidental cysts are benign findings.
items.kp: Fast hard elderly neck mass: fear anaplastic cancer.

items.q: MEN2A combines medullary thyroid cancer with which two tumours classically?
o: Mucosal neuromas and marfanoid habitus alone
items.exp: MEN2A (RET) unites medullary thyroid carcinoma, phaeochromocytoma and parathyroid hyperplasia. MEN2B adds mucosal neuromas and marfanoid habitus without parathyroid disease typically.
r: Incorrect. That pituitary grouping belongs to MEN1.
Correct. Phaeo plus parathyroid plus medullary equals MEN2A.
Incorrect. Pancreatic tumours belong to MEN1 Wermer syndrome.
Incorrect. Neuromas define MEN2B, which usually spares parathyroids.
items.kp: MEN2A: medullary, phaeo, parathyroid. Screen RET families.
